sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Narrow market breadth persists as only 4 of 11 sectors maintain all-green status, led by dominant momentum in Energy and Technology, while defensive and cyclical laggards continue to drag.

Market breadth remains highly concentrated, with only four sectors—Energy, Technology, Healthcare, and Financials—demonstrating "all-green" positive performance across weekly, monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, and YTD timeframes. Energy continues to lead the entire market with a dominant momentum score of 0.92, while Technology follows closely at 0.83. Healthcare shows the most consistent medium-term backing, standing out as the only sector with sustained top-three ranking strength across the 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons.

Rotational activity is minimal but shows minor shifts. Financials and Utilities were the sole gainers over the last five sessions, each climbing +1 spot in the rankings. Conversely, Real Estate and Communication Services are fading, both slipping -1 spot. Momentum remains severely depressed at the bottom of the board, anchored by Consumer Cyclical at a weak 0.12 momentum score.

## Strength
* **Concentrated Breadth:** Only 4 of 11 groups are all-green across all time horizons, highlighting a highly bifurcated market.
* **Energy and Tech Lead:** Energy (momentum 0.92, rank 1) and Technology (momentum 0.83, rank 2) remain the primary engines of market strength.
* **Sustained Healthcare:** Healthcare (momentum 0.75, rank 5) is the only sector exhibiting sustained strength, holding a top-three rank across the 1-, 3-, and 6-month periods.
* **Financials Join Strong Cohort:** Financials (momentum 0.68) maintain all-green status, supported by recent upward ranking movement.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Financials and Utilities Edge Up:** Financials (+1 spot to rank 6, momentum 0.68) and Utilities (+1 spot to rank 9, momentum 0.28) are the only sectors to improve their rankings over the past 5 sessions.
* **Communication and Real Estate Slip:** Communication Services (-1 spot to rank 10, momentum 0.28) and Real Estate (-1 spot to rank 7, momentum 0.30) represent the week's primary decliners.
* **Severe Cyclical Lag:** Consumer Cyclical remains the absolute momentum laggard with a score of 0.12, firmly rooted at rank 11.

## Divergences
* **No Fragile All-Green Signals:** No early-warning fragile all-green status or ranking disagreements were detected among the leading sectors.
* **Basic Materials Disconnect:** Basic Materials holds a strong momentum score of 0.67 (rank 3), yet it fails to achieve all-green status, indicating near-term friction despite its high YTD ranking.

Confirmation would be the sector maintaining its upward trajectory during broader market consolidation, while invalidation would be a breakdown below recent swing lows, indicating a false relative breakout.

industries.note:
# US Industries Daily Note: September 4, 2026

**TL;DR:** Market breadth remains highly concentrated with only 22 of 144 groups in all-green status, led by dominant energy and technology hardware, while retail and regional banking stage a sharp upward rotation against fading travel and metals.

Market leadership continues to be anchored by a select group of high-momentum sectors. Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (momentum 0.984) and Computer Hardware (momentum 0.962) lead the 22 "all-green" industries, showing sustained strength across 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons alongside Marine Shipping (momentum 0.927) and Biotechnology (momentum 0.873). 

A powerful weekly rotation is underway in retail and financial services. Department Stores surged 30 spots to rank 77, and Specialty Retail jumped 21 spots to rank 83, while Regional Banks (+13 spots) and Life Insurance (+13 spots) also posted notable gains. Conversely, defensive and travel-related sectors are fading rapidly, with Insurance Brokers falling 18 spots, Travel Services dropping 14 spots, and Lodging and Residential Construction both sliding 12 spots.

## Strength
* **Concentrated Breadth:** Only 22 of 144 industry groups (15.3%) are "all-green," showing positive performance across weekly, monthly, quarterly, half-year, and YTD windows.
* **Top-Tier Leadership:** Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (YTD rank 2) and Computer Hardware (YTD rank 1) maintain near-perfect momentum scores of 0.984 and 0.962, respectively.
* **Sustained Performers:** Marine Shipping (momentum 0.927), Biotechnology (momentum 0.873), Semiconductors (momentum 0.833), and Diversified Banks (momentum 0.83) continue to exhibit robust, multi-month strength.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Retail and Banking Rebounds:** Department Stores (+30 spots, rank 77, momentum 0.73) and Specialty Retail (+21 spots, rank 83, momentum 0.47) led the weekly gainers, supported by Regional Banks (+13 spots to rank 57, momentum 0.70).
* **Steepest Declines:** Insurance Brokers (-18 spots to rank 108, momentum 0.38) and Travel Services (-14 spots to rank 116, momentum 0.31) experienced the largest rank drops over the last 5 sessions.
* **Momentum Laggards:** Footwear & Accessories (momentum 0.038, YTD rank 142) and Advertising Agencies (momentum 0.120, YTD rank 144) remain anchored at the bottom of the market.

## Divergences
* **Fading Leaders:** High-momentum metal and medical groups are showing early signs of fatigue, with Copper (momentum 0.74) slipping 7 spots, Other Industrial Metals & Mining (momentum 0.68) dropping 5 spots, and Gold (momentum 0.73) down 3 spots.
* **Emerging Low-Momentum Gainers:** Specialty Retail (+21 spots, momentum 0.47) and Utilities - Renewable (+16 spots, momentum 0.36) are jumping in rank from low momentum bases, indicating early-stage accumulation.
* **Consumer Staples Rotation:** Discount Stores (+10 spots, momentum 0.37) and Auto Parts (+10 spots, momentum 0.43) are quietly moving up the rankings despite mediocre overall momentum scores.
